nodes.label: Database Regression Suite
nodes.rationale: Automated checks that schema.sql, seed.sql and migrations behave the way docs/DATABASE.md says they do; each file builds its own database so suites run in parallel and a failure cannot cascade.

nodes.label: PGlite Test Engine
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL compiled to WebAssembly: same planner, constraint machinery and SQLSTATE codes. Chosen because almost everything asserted is enforced by the database - a hand-written mock would accept SQL that PostgreSQL rejects, so a suite built on one would pass while proving nothing. Bundles PG16 while Supabase runs 15+.

nodes.label: Supabase Auth Shim In The Harness
nodes.rationale: tests/helpers/db.ts supplies auth.users, auth.uid(), the authenticated/anon roles and Supabase GRANTs. The shim lives in the harness and never in schema.sql so the file under test stays byte-for-byte the file pasted into the Supabase SQL Editor; auth.uid() reads a session setting so RLS tests can switch identity.

nodes.label: schema.test.ts
nodes.rationale: Application, idempotency, table/RLS structure, SECURITY DEFINER helpers, updated_at triggers, documented indexes, and migration convergence.

nodes.label: Schema Idempotency Test
nodes.rationale: The single most valuable test in the file: schema.sql is pasted by hand into the SQL Editor and a half-applied run gets pasted again. An earlier version declared the RLS helper functions before public.profiles existed and failed on first apply - that class of bug is what this catches.

nodes.label: constraints.test.ts
nodes.rationale: Generated columns compute, recompute and cannot be spoofed; predictions_result_matches_status from both directions; domain CHECKs, FKs, cascade/restrict, updated_at triggers and explanation ranking.

nodes.label: leakage.test.ts
nodes.rationale: Leakage is silent - nothing crashes, the metrics just look great and the model is worthless - so the schema fights it structurally and these tests check the structure holds. Includes an automated audit for outcome-shaped column names that is itself checked not to forbid legitimate elapsed-time features.

nodes.label: seed.test.ts
nodes.rationale: Asserts rather than trusts that every seeded row is unmistakably fictional ([DEMO] names, DEMO- codes), because the naming convention is the only thing stopping a dashboard screenshot being mistaken for real land acquisition figures. Also asserts no fabricated model results.

nodes.label: rls.test.ts
nodes.rationale: The full policy matrix exercised as each role, plus privilege-escalation attempts from every angle; self-promotion is rejected by the policy WITH CHECK raising 42501 rather than a CHECK violation.

nodes.label: SET ROLE Is Required For RLS Tests
nodes.rationale: PGlite connects as a superuser and PostgreSQL exempts superusers and table owners from RLS entirely, so a policy test that forgot to switch role would pass unconditionally while proving nothing. Every assertion runs through actingAs / actingAsAnon in helpers/identity.ts.

nodes.label: Assert On SQLSTATE, Not Message Text
nodes.rationale: Error codes are stable across PostgreSQL versions and locales; messages are not. Where a specific constraint is the point of the test, err.constraint is asserted too.

nodes.label: expectSqlError Negative-Test Helper
nodes.rationale: Throws if the statement unexpectedly succeeds, so a guard that stops working fails loudly rather than passing quietly - a bare try/catch cannot tell those two apart.

nodes.label: Never Compare Two Wall-Clock Readings
nodes.rationale: NOW() returns the transaction timestamp and PGlite's clock has millisecond resolution, so two fast statements can share a tick. The updated_at tests backdate the row with the trigger disabled and assert the trigger moved it forward - deterministic and a stricter test besides.

nodes.label: What The Database Suite Does Not Cover
nodes.rationale: Real Supabase Auth JWTs (auth.uid() is shimmed), the backend authorization layer (the Node backend uses the service role key and bypasses RLS), and performance (indexes are asserted to exist, not to be used).
